rules_evaluated.evidence: Module Big Idea (earn-the-trust.md line 6): 'Two curated skills from the frontier do the security work, one skill you author through conversation with Claude does the quality work.' This exercise's title ('Map the access surface, own the delta') and 'The point' (line 11): 'The curated skill does the breadth; you own the codebase-specific judgment the skill can't have' instantiate exactly the curated-security half of that Big Idea — invoke the frontier skill for breadth, then supply the codebase judgment the skill structurally can't have. 'What you build' (line 9) names the delta, not the raw skill output, as the artifact — matches the Big Idea's framing that the skill does the work and the student's judgment is the value-add. Correctly scoped as the opening beat of a three-exercise module mood, not a full resolution — file ends on 'What this sets up' (lines 83-85), handing the mood forward to STRIDE (Ex2) rather than closing it here. One-sentence state-and-setup test satisfied: student leaves trusting the skill's breadth while owning final judgment themselves; that ownership is what Ex2's bigger call (picking the one threat worth hardening) needs next.

M3's mood — both the strategy doc's Mood arc and this exercise's own Meta block — is 'earned trust', not 'unease', so the rule's diagnostic target doesn't fire on this surface. Checked regardless: no punitive framing present anywhere in the file. 'Push back until the reason names your codebase' (lines 72-74) and the trainer push-back block ('is that reason true for this codebase, or true for any codebase?', line 108) frame sharpening as coaching-toward-specificity, not having-done-wrong.
